title: Pool oversight sparkline + quickburst editor
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact "Pool Oversight" panel that combines a high-density sparkline health view with an inline QuickBurst editor to set temporary burst parameters. Goal: surface needle-in-time health signals and let operators launch short bursts without leaving the dashboard. Focus on compactness for the dedicated capacity HUD and consistency with existing telemetry canvases.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Maya Patel created initial PRD sketch; motivation: reduce context-switch for ops when reacting to transient load spikes. Included requirements: sparkline, peak detection indicator, inline burst modal, rollback CTA, accessibility color contrasts.

2025-01-20 - Design review: flagged trade-offs between inline editing and accidental burst triggers. Decided to use a confirmation toast + 5s undo window. Request from ENG to expose burst params as an API for automation.
2025-01-27 - Prototype updated (Figma v3): added micro-confirmation flow and 'simulate' toggle to preview cost impact. PM (Carlos Rivera) requested added per-token cost estimate for burst duration.

2025-01-30 - Eng sync (Priya Shen): feasibility OK, but KV cache eviction behavior during burst needs coordination. Engineering asked for explicit fields: burst_gpu_count, burst_ttl_seconds, priority_tier and a 'dry_run' mode in API.
2025-02-03 - Usability session with 4 SREs: positive feedback on sparkline mini-annotations; concern about clutter with many pools—added collapse/minimap behavior to address density.
2025-02-08 - Preparing final review: handoff notes created, redlines for dev in Confluence, accessibility checklist completed, and a follow-up ticket requested for telemetry instrumentation.
